summary.headline: Saregama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR3,143 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 39% to INR1,180 million.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR3,143 million (+37% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of INR1,180 million (+39%) and operational PBT of INR858 million (+43%). The music vertical (licensing, artist management, retail) grew 35% YoY to INR2,513 million, with EBITDA of INR1,540 million. Management repeatedly asked investors to judge performance on a rolling 12-month basis, citing a low base in H1 FY26. The video vertical revenue fell 16% to INR183 million as the film business is wound down in favour of Bhansali Productions.

financial_highlights.metric: Music vertical revenue (licensing, artist management, retail)

financial_highlights.change: up from 48.4% YoY (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Music (licensing, artist management, retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,513 million (+35% YoY), EBITDA INR1,540 million (+37%), net profit INR1,165 million (+46%). Retail (Carvaan) about INR21 crore in the quarter per analyst's reading of the presentation; management confirmed the INR200 crore segment figure is licensing plus retail, with artist management reported separately.

segments.name: Video
segments.commentary: Revenue INR183 million, down 16% YoY, reflecting a deliberate wind-down of the film business in favour of investment in Bhansali Productions. Management expects further decline in coming quarters.

segments.name: Live events
segments.commentary: Management did not disclose segment revenue in the prepared remarks. Analyst cited events revenue of INR45 crore in Q2 and INR61 crore in H1 FY27 (vs FY26 INR62 crore), and the division made a loss in Q2 as IP-based event launch costs are expensed, not capitalised.

segments.name: Pocket Aces (investee)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even in FY26 and is moving towards profitability in FY27. Its talent business is combined with Saregama artist management, with no split disclosed.

segments.name: Bhansali Productions (investee)
segments.commentary: Biggest release, Love & War, is slated for Q4 FY27. Slate for FY28 is being worked on. Music rights for its content are being purchased under a separate deal.

guidance_outlook: Music vertical revenue CAGR guidance maintained at 20% to 23% on a 3-to-5-year basis, not per year (management reiterated, and said it will not guide by vertical).
Music vertical EBITDA margin guidance of 60% to 65% over the short-to-medium run maintained.
New content spend for FY27 guided at INR300 crore to INR350 crore (midpoint INR325 crore), with content budgets rising about 10% per annum; combined FY28-FY30 new content spend around INR1,200 crore.
Management expects EBITDA and profit growth to follow revenue as content bought 2-4 years ago contributes positive margins; new music retains a 5-year payback and 55-75 years of returns.
Pricing growth in Indian subscription is expected to start in roughly 2 to 3 years.
Carvaan app is in test phase; management will run experiments through FY27 and promised more detail by year-end or in 4-6 months.
capex_capacity: Content investment: new content spend guided at INR300-350 crore for FY27, with a 5-year payback on each new music acquisition.
Catalogue of 180,000+ songs, adding 4,500-5,000 new releases a year.
Live events: Carvaan Live produced 54 shows serving about 10,000 attendees in Q2; Ilaiyaraaja US tour covered 11 cities with 20,000 attendees; 17 devotional shows held.
Management will keep increasing live events investment and shift the mix toward owned IP (UN40, HaHaKaar, Krishna, Carvaan Live) from artist-based concerts.
Around 100 hours of AI-assisted podcast content planned for Q3 FY27.
Artist roster of 340 artists with a combined follower base above 450 million on Instagram and YouTube.
demand_pricing: Management says India is 1% of global recorded music (USD31.7 billion in 2025, IFPI) and is the most under-penetrated large music market; paid subscription growth in India currently comes entirely from new subscribers.
60% of FY26 music revenue came from music released after 2000.
Short-format video platforms (YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels) remain on fixed-fee deals; no move to ad-share yet.
Non-digital revenue (TV, radio, brand, public performance) is a minority; brand and public performance are the only non-digital lines growing decently. Digital split not quantified.
Over 20 brand deals signed in Q2 with partners including Apple, Airbnb, Google, Cadbury and Tanishq.
Management said AI-generated music is winning on volume but not listenership; unlicensed AI covers are the main near-term issue, handled via tracking and buyouts or takedowns.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a loss in events despite reasonable revenue, and why did unallocable expenses rise to INR27 crore from INR18 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IP-based events carry higher upfront costs that are fully expensed. The unallocable cost increase reflects other income (interest on QIP money, now invested in Pocket Aces, Haryanvi catalogue and Bhansali) falling 55% YoY; excluding that, it was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 music guidance of 20-23% conservative when H1 grew about 37%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is given on a 3-to-5-year CAGR basis and not per year; some years may be higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the music segment margin expansion (EBIT margin 48.4% to 55.4%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said content acquired in FY24-FY26 is now past its charge-off stage, so revenue growth from that content exceeds amortisation. Paid subscription is growing much faster than ad-supported, with higher yield per paid listen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 live events pipeline, and is Diljit Dosanjh touring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there will be no Diljit Dosanjh show this season due to financials. Pipeline includes a Guru Randhawa show, UN40, HaHaKaar and another artist tour yet to be announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current liabilities rise by over INR100 crore, aiding H1 operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Abhishek Kapoor said customer advances received under deals, recognised over time, drove the increase in current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the content spend guidance beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 new content spend is INR300-350 crore, rising about 10% a year, for a combined FY28-FY30 spend of around INR1,200 crore. The Bhansali music deal is a separate arrangement and is included in this pool.

risks_watch: Video vertical revenue likely to fall further as film wind-down and Bhansali transition play out.
Other income down 55% YoY, which lifts unallocable costs; the FY27 earnings base depends on operating growth.
Events profitability: IP-based events are expensed upfront and may keep depressing margins near term.
Quarterly volatility: management asked investors to judge on rolling 12-month figures, and quarterly numbers can move with release timing and marketing spend.
Short-format platform monetisation remains fixed-fee; a shift to ad-share is not yet agreed.
Unlicensed AI covers and remakes of catalogue songs remain a near-term infringement risk.
Carvaan app and community monetisation remain untested; no subscriber metrics disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term music thesis and margin inflection, but defensive on quarter-on-quarter moves in other income, unallocable costs and segment reporting, asking investors to use rolling 12-month figures. Management declined to quantify digital/non-digital split, Carvaan app metrics and short-form deal terms, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: Please evaluate our performance only on a rolling 12-month basis.
We are entering that cycle now, where content that was bought 2, 3 or 4 years ago is starting to contribute positive margins.
So we have only one trigger for growth, which is the addition of new subscribers.
Saregama may be the cleanest listed way to own this thesis.

adds.what: New content spend INR300-350 crore for FY27 (catalogue acquisition, not physical capacity)

growth.why: Music vertical revenue CAGR guidance of 20-23% over 3-5 years was held, with Q2 revenue up 37% and music up 35%; backing is a rising content spend (INR300-350 crore in FY27, about INR1,200 crore over FY28-30) and a 180,000+ song catalogue, but no physical capacity is involved and the guidance is a multi-year CAGR rather than a per-year target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Music EBIT margin rose to 55.4% from 48.4% YoY as FY24-FY26 content passed its charge-off stage, and management maintains a 60-65% music EBITDA margin guide over the short-to-medium run, though Q2 music EBITDA margin was about 61% (INR1,540m on INR2,513m) and events losses weigh on the total.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Music revenue grew 35% YoY and 4,500-5,000 new releases a year are being added to a 180,000+ song catalogue, with 20+ brand deals signed in Q2, but the 20-23% guide is a 3-5 year CAGR and not a per-year target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; the only investment is catalogue content spend of INR300-350 crore in FY27 and around INR1,200 crore over FY28-30, which is not capex and is already guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 growth was about 37% against the 20-23% multi-year CAGR guide, but management held guidance and said it does not guide per year, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Music CAGR and EBITDA margin guidance were both held, and Q2 revenue rose 37% YoY and EBITDA 39%, so no cut is signalled, although video revenue (-16%) and events losses are headwinds.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 100 hours of AI-assisted podcast content are planned for Q3 FY27, Bhansali's Love & War is slated for Q4 FY27, and the Carvaan app is in test with more detail due in 4-6 months.

rows.label: Bhansali Productions slate and Love & War release
rows.why: Biggest Bhansali release Love & War is slated for Q4 FY27 and the FY28 slate is being worked on, though video revenue fell 16% to INR183m and is expected to decline further.

rows.label: Indian subscription pricing growth
rows.why: Management expects pricing growth in Indian subscription to start in roughly 2-3 years, and paid subscriber growth currently comes entirely from new subscribers, so there is no near-term pricing lever.

rows.label: Live events: owned-IP shift and upfront cost drag
rows.why: Events made a loss in Q2 on INR45 crore revenue because IP-based launch costs are expensed, and management will raise events investment and shift mix to owned IP (UN40, HaHaKaar, Krishna, Carvaan Live), which may keep margins depressed near term.
